correctness.rationale: For n>=4 the selected K(n,2) vertices are precisely edges of a graph F on [n]. Every 2-set in [n] must be disjoint from a selected edge, so total domination is equivalent to vertex-cover number tau(F)>=3. Inclusion-minimality forces tau(F)=3 and tau(F-e)<=2 for every edge. The critical-tau=2 lemma gives 2K2 or K3. If a vertex has degree>=3, deleting it and using incident-edge criticality forces the K3 case with all three neighbors, hence K4; the matching case is impossible by two-cover cardinality. For maximum degree<=2, edge-critical connected components are K2 and odd cycles, leaving only 3K2, K3+K2, C5. Their labeled support counts give 15*C(n,6),10*C(n,5),12*C(n,5),C(n,4) at sizes 3,4,5,6. At n=4 this reduces to z^6. The log-concavity difference at size four is 10*C(n,5)^2*(25-3n), and the size-three/four ratio (n-5)/4 gives the nonunimodality threshold at n=10. Independently enumerated all selected-vertex subsets for n=4,5,6: {6:1}; {4:10,5:12,6:5}; {3:15,4:60,5:72,6:15}. Finite checks corroborate but do not prove the unrestricted classification.
